title: AI Coding and Technical Debt
summary: Plugin developer on technical debt from vibe-coded products; experience determines how much debt accrues.

assertions.quote: the lack of upfront work that you're putting in is going to make it more difficult down the line

verdicts.note: Unreviewed, fast AI output does accumulate debt (GitClear duplication, churn), but debt depends on review discipline, not on whether AI was used per se.
In 302k AI-authored commits, 22.7% of AI-introduced issues persist, and surviving debt grew past 100k issues. But there's no human-written baseline, so 'more than hand-built' is untested.

assertions.quote: If you're an experienced coder ... you're probably going to have a lot less technical debt

verdicts.note: Experts get more reliable results and catch errors, but several RCTs show larger measured speedups for juniors, and METR found experts slowed; contested.

assertions.quote: you're also going to be dealing with all the other aspects like the release and the protection

verdicts.note: Unreviewed AI-built apps commonly ship with security, scaling and maintainability problems; prototypes are their sweet spot.
The 47-source review finds evidence strongest for prototyping and UI work and weakest for production. The break-down half is mostly unstudied, not shown.
